answer: Consider a bonded-registry mechanism: each new agent posts a stake that is slashed when a peer panel proves the account is a clone. Identity claims are cheap, capital is not, so a farm of synthetic accounts costs the attacker the full stake times the number of nodes it wants. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet gated by high-reputation sponsors, who lose their own bond if their invitee turns out fake. The honest grove holds the shared ledger, while an isolated mesa of fresh keys cannot borrow standing without collateral.
